game: CLE@PIT Week 6 2025, kickoff 2025-10-12 13:00 ET, outdoor, PIT -5.5, total 37.5

script.base: Low-total home favorite game: Pittsburgh leads by halftime in a grind (implied PIT 21.5 / CLE 16.0) and mixes Warren and Gainwell late to protect a one-score lead. Cleveland, a 5.5-point dog, throws more once behind; Flacco faces a 43% PIT blitz and his EPA/dropback vs blitz is -0.47, so the ball comes out short instead of chasing Jeudy's 288 air yards. Pace stays slow. Weather not in the pack, so no wind/rain lean.
script.flip1: Divisional game stays close or Cleveland leads. Judkins keeps a 20-carry script (62 carries, 286 rush yards in weeks 3-5), Pittsburgh cannot just clock-kill, and Rodgers has to throw with Austin out, which flips PIT RB unders and any CLE rush-under idea.
script.flip2: Pittsburgh blows it open early. Warren/Gainwell clock-kill carries spike and late starter receiving snaps stall, while Cleveland garbage-time dropbacks boost short targets but Judkins's rush line dies.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse injury report only; final inactives not in the pack. CLE DT Mike Hall Jr. Out (knee) softens the interior Pittsburgh runs into, a small plus for Warren/Gainwell and a nick against any PIT rush under. PIT WR Calvin Austin III Out (shoulder) removes 11 targets, 69 yards and 164 air yards from weeks 2-4; same-position leftover is DK Metcalf (15 targets, 178 yards) with Jonnu Smith (10/56) as the short-area spillover, but no line-move history to confirm a sleeper. PIT CB Jalen Ramsey Questionable (hamstring) is a game-time flag, not an out: if he sits, Jeudy/Bond face an unnamed backup and any CLE outside under is damaged. No Cleveland skill player is listed out; Judkins remains the back (Ford 6/17, Sampson 3/-4 in the same window).

Pittsburgh's middle bleed (CLE allows 11.5 YPA on a tiny sample) would fit Smith/Warren more than Metcalf.

form: Windows are asymmetric and used as labeled: CLE offense weeks 3-5, PIT offense weeks 2-4, prop logs as last-games. Jeudy last4 51, 17, 48, 15; 17+48+15=80 matches the week 3-5 total, so the recent three are all under 48.5 and the 51 is the older game. Judkins receiving last4 10, 1, 33, 18; 1+33+18=52 matches the week 3-5 total (about 17.3 per game vs a 14.5 line), with a 1-yard dud inside the window. Njoku week 3-5 is 118 yards (about 39.3) vs a 40.5 line. Judkins rush week 3-5 is 94, 82, 110. Warren's week 2-4 line (32 carries, 95 yards) does not reconcile with prop logs 37, 48, 47, so his form is not treated as clean. Gainwell week 2-4 rush 20+16+99=135, so the 99 is recent, not an old spike. Metcalf week 2-4 is 20, 32, 126 vs 57.5.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because Pittsburgh did not blitz at 43% or Flacco beat it with one right-side shot, Jeudy posted another 50-plus like the older 51 against a limited Ramsey or a backup, and the checkdowns went to Njoku (19 targets, 118 yards in the window) and Fannin (14 targets) so Judkins repeated the 1-yard receiving game. A close divisional script that just hands Judkins 20 carries also zeros the receiving over without making Jeudy useful. That counter is strong enough to keep both at lean and unsized, not strong enough to erase the blitz-efficiency read.
slip_story: One pressure-slog story in a 37.5 game: Flacco checks down (Judkins recyds over) and cannot cash Jeudy's deep air yards (recyds under). They win together when the blitz gets home. Do not add a CLE team-total over, a Jeudy over, or a Njoku over on the same slip. Shared kill is a no-blitz or Ramsey-out game that lets the explosive through.
